wine_name: Terroir Al Limit Les Tosses, Catalunya

hook.note: Mentions 'granite-and-slate' but ground truth specifies llicorella (slate) without granite; score claims (97 points) not verifiable from context which only says '6 entries (medals/points)' without specifics.

wine_summary.note: Accurate on grape, philosophy, and style; 97-point claim across vintages not verifiable from provided context; otherwise well-aligned with ground truth on winemaking direction and terroir.

terroir_expression.note: Correctly identifies llicorella, steep slopes, altitude, Mediterranean climate; doesn't mention the specific 600m elevation or 90-year-old vines, but nothing fabricated; 'quartzite' is a minor addition not in ground truth but plausible for Priorat.

vinification_summary.note: Ground truth says recent vintages ferment and age in cement tanks with no wood aging; the model describes 8 months oak élevage as the core method, which directly contradicts the verified winemaking approach of dispensing with oak entirely.

food_pairing.note: Pairings are logical and well-reasoned for a firm, tannic, herbal Carignan; Nashville hot chicken is a creative and defensible pick; no factual errors.

comparable_wines.note: All three are legitimate Priorat comparisons, but none are pure Carignan like Les Tosses, which somewhat weakens the comparison; Manyetes is actually Carignan-dominant so that's a good pick, but calling it 'Grenache-led' may be inaccurate.

style_profile.note: Accurate and concise; correctly identifies 100% Carignan, body, tannin structure, and mineral character.

cellar_recommendation.note: 8-12 year window is reasonable but somewhat conservative for a wine with 97-point scores and ageworthy structure from old vines; no fabricated specifics though.

value_assessment.note: Price range of $120-$180 is not provided in context and may be fabricated; comparisons to Clos Mogador and Clos Erasmus are reasonable but price accuracy is unverifiable.

market_position.note: Positioning is accurate and well-articulated; aligns with the wine's profile as a terroir-driven, collector-oriented Priorat.

insider_take.note: Strong, opinionated take that correctly positions the wine as architectural rather than powerful; Etna Rosso and Barolo comparisons are apt for the style; no banned words, direct and specific.

overall_note: Strong voice throughout with no banned words; main correctness issue is the vinification_summary contradicting ground truth by emphasizing oak aging when the winery has moved to cement with no wood, and unverifiable score/price claims in several fields.
